title: XML encoding scanning in XML documents is not interoperable

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

labels.name: topic: xml
labels.description: The XML syntax and parser, DOMParser and XMLSerializer with XML, and XSLT and XPath

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/1752 added scanning for XML encoding declarations inside HTML documents: the spec's [get an XML encoding](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#concept-get-xml-encoding-when-sniffing) algorithm.

It is called from called from [prescan a byte stream to determine an encoding](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#prescan-a-byte-stream-to-determine-its-encoding), called from the [encoding sniffing algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#encoding-sniffing-algorithm), which is explicitly in the [HTML parser section](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#the-input-byte-stream), which says

> For XML documents, the algorithm user agents are required to use to determine the character encoding is given by XML. This section does not apply to XML documents.

---

For XML documents, the spec's guidance is located in the [Loading XML documents](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#read-xml) section, which says

> user agents must follow the requirements defined in XML and Namespaces in XML, XML Media Types, DOM, and other relevant specifications to [create and initialize a Document object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#initialise-the-document-object) document, given "xml", type, and navigationParams, and return that [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document).

and later

> The actual HTTP headers and other metadata, not the headers as mutated or implied by the algorithms given in this specification, are the ones that must be used when determining the character encoding according to the rules given in the above specifications. Once the character encoding is established, the [document's character encoding](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-encoding) must be set to that character encoding.

In practice, none of the browsers strictly follow the XML spec (which has [some minimal first-4-bytes sniffing](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-guessing)) or RFC 7303; they all have more extensive sniffing. But, that more-extensive sniffing is not interoperable:

| Initial processing instruction | Blink | Gecko | WebKit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<?xmlfoo encoding="windows-1251"?>` | windows-1251 | UTF-8 | windows-1251 |
| `<?xmlfoo version="1.0" encoding="windows-1251"?>` | windows-1251 | windows-1251 | windows-1251 |
| `<?xmlfoo version "1.0" encoding "windows-1251"?>` | UTF-8 | windows-1251 | UTF-8 |

Note that these are all well-formed PIs, so per the XML specs the correct answer is UTF-8 in all cases. (But nobody implements that.)

According to GPT-6 Astra Extra High, Blink and WebKit code are basically the same, except Blink uses signed `char`s, so inserting byte 0x80 around `=` is accepted by Blink and rejected by WebKit, which is fun. But basically, they use the same [get an XML encoding](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#concept-get-xml-encoding-when-sniffing)  algorithm in XML as in HTML, just with some other steps before/after. Gecko is fairly different, thus the results here.
